title: 2 Samuel Chapter 8 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Samuel chapter 8 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 8 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Samuel Chapter 8.

questions.question: Who did David smite and subdue, taking Methegammah out of their hand?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 8:1 states that David smote the Philistines and took Methegammah out of their hand.

questions.question: How did David measure the Moabites to decide who should be put to death and who should live?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 8:2 explains that David measured the Moabites with a line to determine who to kill and who to keep alive.

questions.question: True or False: The Moabites became servants to David and brought him gifts.
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 8:2 clearly says the Moabites became David's servants and brought gifts.

questions.question: Who was the king of Zobah that David smote as he went to recover his border?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 8:3 identifies Hadadezer, son of Rehob, king of Zobah as the king David smote.

questions.question: How many chariots did David take from Hadadezer?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 8:4 states David took a thousand chariots from Hadadezer.

questions.question: What did David do to most of the chariot horses he captured?
options: Houghed all except for a hundred
questions.correctAnswer: Houghed all except for a hundred
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 8:4 says David houghed all the chariot horses but reserved a hundred.

questions.question: When the Syrians of Damascus came to help Hadadezer, how many Syrian men did David kill?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 8:5 records that David slew twenty-two thousand Syrian men.

questions.question: True or False: David put garrisons in Syria of Damascus, and the Syrians became servants to him and brought gifts.
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 8:6 confirms David put garrisons in Damascus and the Syrians became servants and brought gifts.

questions.question: Who preserved David wherever he went according to 2 Samuel 8?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 8:6 states the LORD preserved David whithersoever he went.

questions.question: True or False: David took the shields of iron from Hadadezer's servants and brought them to Jerusalem.
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 8:7 says David took the shields of gold, not iron, from Hadadezer's servants.

questions.question: From which cities of Hadadezer did David take much brass?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 8:8 mentions Betah and Berothai as the cities from which David took much brass.

questions.question: Which king sent his son Joram to salute and bless David for smiting Hadadezer?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 8:9-10 shows Toi king of Hamath sent Joram to salute and bless David.

questions.question: What did Joram bring with him to David?
options: Vessels of silver, gold, and brass
questions.correctAnswer: Vessels of silver, gold, and brass
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 8:10 records that Joram brought vessels of silver, gold, and brass.

questions.question: In what order did these events happen in 2 Samuel 8? 1) David smote the Philistines, 2) David smote Hadadezer, 3) David put garrisons in Edom, 4) Toi sent Joram to David. Which came first?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 8:1 comes before 8:3, 8:14, and 8:9, so David smote the Philistines first.

questions.question: True or False: David reigned over all Israel and executed judgment and justice unto all his people.
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 8:15 confirms David's reign over all Israel and his administration of judgment and justice.

medium.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 8 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Samuel Chapter 8 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did David take from the servants of Hadadezer and bring to Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 8:7 states that David took the shields of gold from Hadadezer's servants and brought them to Jerusalem.

questions.question: From which cities did David take exceeding much brass?
questions.explanation: According to 2 Samuel 8:8, David took a great amount of brass from Betah and Berothai, cities of Hadadezer.

questions.question: How did Toi king of Hamath respond upon hearing of David's victory over Hadadezer?
options: Sent his son Joram to salute and bless David
questions.correctAnswer: Sent his son Joram to salute and bless David
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 8:9-10 describe how Toi sent his son Joram to greet David and bless him because Hadadezer had been at war with Toi, and David defeated Hadadezer.

questions.question: What kinds of vessels did Joram bring with him to David?
options: Vessels of silver, gold, and brass
questions.correctAnswer: Vessels of silver, gold, and brass
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 8:10 states Joram brought vessels of silver, gold, and brass to David when he came to salute him.

questions.question: What did David do with the silver and gold he dedicated from all nations he subdued?
options: Used them to build a palace
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 8:11 explains that David dedicated the silver and gold he had taken from nations to the LORD, showing his faith and gratitude.

questions.question: Which nations are listed as those from whom David took spoil and dedicated it to the LORD?
options: Syria, Moab, Ammon, Philistines, Amalek, and Zobah
Egypt, Edom, Canaan, Syria, Moab, Ammon
Philistines, Edom, Israel, Judah, Moab, Ammon
Amalek, Egypt, Babylon, Syria, Moab, Philistines
questions.correctAnswer: Syria, Moab, Ammon, Philistines, Amalek, and Zobah
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 8:12 lists these specific nations as those from whom David took spoil and dedicated it to the LORD.

questions.question: How does 2 Samuel 8:11-12 teach about the virtue of generosity and worship in practical Christian living?
options: It shows that dedicating spoils to God expresses gratitude and acknowledges His sovereignty.
It teaches that all wealth should be kept for personal gain.
It encourages ignoring God in times of victory.
It suggests giving only to earthly rulers.
questions.correctAnswer: It shows that dedicating spoils to God expresses gratitude and acknowledges His sovereignty.
questions.explanation: Verses 11 and 12 illustrate David's dedication of spoils to the LORD, emphasizing gratitude, worship, and recognition of God's provision, which are key Christian virtues.

questions.question: What promise is implied in 2 Samuel 8:6 and 2 Samuel 8:14 regarding the LORD's protection over David?
options: The LORD preserved David wherever he went, ensuring his success and safety.
David was left to his own devices without divine help.
David lost many battles despite his faith.
The LORD only helped David in Israel, not abroad.
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD preserved David wherever he went, ensuring his success and safety.
questions.explanation: Verses 6 and 14 together emphasize that the LORD preserved David wherever he went, showing divine protection and blessing for obedience and faith.

questions.question: Based on 2 Samuel 8:9-10, how can believers apply the principle of humility and blessing towards others who have conflicts with their own enemies?
options: By showing respect and offering blessings to those who oppose their foes, promoting peace and goodwill.
By attacking anyone who associates with their enemies.
By ignoring all outside nations regardless of circumstances.
By retaliating with hatred against all enemies.
questions.correctAnswer: By showing respect and offering blessings to those who oppose their foes, promoting peace and goodwill.
questions.explanation: Toi’s sending of Joram to bless David, who fought his enemy, models humility and peace-making even among complex conflicts, a biblical virtue.

questions.question: What role did Joab have according to 2 Samuel 8:16?
options: Over the host (commander of the army)
questions.correctAnswer: Over the host (commander of the army)
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 8:16 clearly states that Joab, son of Zeruiah, was over the host, meaning he was the commander of David's army.

questions.question: Who were the priests mentioned in 2 Samuel 8:17?
options: Zadok son of Ahitub and Ahimelech son of Abiathar
questions.correctAnswer: Zadok son of Ahitub and Ahimelech son of Abiathar
questions.explanation: Verse 17 lists Zadok and Ahimelech as the priests serving during David's reign.

questions.question: What position did Benaiah son of Jehoiada hold according to 2 Samuel 8:18?
options: Over both the Cherethites and the Pelethites
questions.correctAnswer: Over both the Cherethites and the Pelethites
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 8:18 identifies Benaiah as the leader over the Cherethites and Pelethites, elite groups in David's service.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Samuel 8:15, David reigned only over Judah and neglected the rest of Israel.
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 8:15 states that David reigned over all Israel and executed judgment and justice to all his people, showing his comprehensive rule.

questions.question: True or False: 2 Samuel 8 teaches that God’s preservation of a leader like David is linked to his faithfulness and obedience.
questions.explanation: Verses 6 and 14 show that the LORD preserved David wherever he went, implying divine favor linked to David’s faithfulness and righteous leadership.

questions.question: True or False: 2 Samuel 8:11 encourages believers to keep their victories and possessions private rather than dedicating them to God.
questions.explanation: Verse 11 clearly states that David dedicated the silver and gold to the LORD, teaching believers to honor God openly with their blessings.

hard.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 8 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Samuel Chapter 8.

questions.question: How many men did David kill when he returned from smiting the Syrians in the valley of salt?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 8:13 states that David smote eighteen thousand men in the valley of salt.

questions.question: What military strategy did David use in Edom after defeating the Syrians?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 8:14 says David put garrisons in Edom and all the people became his servants.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes David's reign over Israel according to 2 Samuel 8:15?
options: He reigned but was often challenged
He reigned and executed judgment and justice
questions.correctAnswer: He reigned and executed judgment and justice
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 8:15 explicitly states that David reigned and executed judgment and justice to all his people.

questions.question: Who was over the host during David's reign as mentioned in 2 Samuel 8?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 8:16 identifies Joab son of Zeruiah as the one over the host.

questions.question: Which two priests served during David's reign according to 2 Samuel 8:17?
options: Zadok son of Ahitub and Ahimelech son of Abiathar
questions.correctAnswer: Zadok son of Ahitub and Ahimelech son of Abiathar
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 8:17 clearly names Zadok and Ahimelech as the priests.

questions.question: Who was over both the Cherethites and the Pelethites?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 8:18 states that Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over both the Cherethites and the Pelethites.

questions.question: What is the significance of the 'valley of salt' where David smote the Syrians?
options: It was a site of abundant salt mines
It symbolized a place of divine judgment
It was a strategic battle location east of the Dead Sea
It was the capital city of Edom
questions.correctAnswer: It was a strategic battle location east of the Dead Sea
questions.explanation: The 'valley of salt' refers to a strategic location east of the Dead Sea where David defeated the Syrians (2 Samuel 8:13). This place is historically known as the Arabah valley, a natural passage and battleground.

questions.question: Which other biblical passage parallels David's establishment of garrisons in Edom and the subjugation of its people?
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 9:15-19 recounts Solomon building and fortifying cities including those in Edom, reflecting the continuity of David's military and administrative policies (2 Samuel 8:14).

questions.question: The Hebrew word for 'garrisons' (מָצוֹד, matsod) in 2 Samuel 8:14 primarily means:
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'matsod' (garrison) denotes a fortified military post or stronghold, indicating David's control over Edom through military presence (2 Samuel 8:14).

questions.question: How does 2 Samuel 8:15 reflect the ideal kingship concept found elsewhere in the Old Testament?
options: It shows a king focused on wealth accumulation
It emphasizes the king's role in judgment and justice
It highlights the king's military conquests only
It stresses the king's isolation from his people
questions.correctAnswer: It emphasizes the king's role in judgment and justice
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 8:15 shows David executing judgment and justice, fulfilling the ideal kingship model seen in passages like Deuteronomy 17:18-20 where the king must be just and lead righteously.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of righteous judgment found in 2 Samuel 8:15?
questions.explanation: Matthew 25:31-46 discusses the final judgment where the righteous are separated from the wicked, echoing the theme of judgment and justice that David executed as king (2 Samuel 8:15).

questions.question: What literary device is evident in the listing of officials and priests serving David in 2 Samuel 8:16-18?
questions.explanation: The listing in 2 Samuel 8:16-18 forms an inclusio framing David's reign by naming military, administrative, and religious officials, showcasing the organized governance under David.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about David's sons according to 2 Samuel 8:18 is correct?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 8:18 states that David's sons were chief rulers, indicating their role in governance during his reign.

questions.question: David's military successes and establishment of garrisons led to a decline in Israel's influence in the region.
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 8:6,14 show that David's victories and garrisons caused surrounding nations like the Syrians and Edomites to become servants to him, increasing Israel's influence rather than diminishing it.

questions.question: What role did Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud serve under King David?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 8:16 identifies Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud as the recorder, responsible for keeping official records during David's reign.

theological.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 8 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Samuel Chapter 8 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is illustrated by David's consistent victories and preservation by the LORD throughout his campaigns?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 8:6 and 2 Samuel 8:14 show that 'the LORD preserved David whithersoever he went,' indicating God's providential care over David's victories, a key doctrine of divine providence.

questions.question: How does 2 Samuel 8:15 demonstrate an essential aspect of godly leadership in the context of theocratic rule?
options: By emphasizing David's role as a judge executing justice
By highlighting the king's military prowess
By focusing on David's wealth accumulation
questions.correctAnswer: By emphasizing David's role as a judge executing justice
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 8:15 states that David 'executed judgment and justice unto all his people,' underscoring the doctrine that godly leadership requires righteous governance and justice in accordance with God's standards.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is revealed by the LORD preserving David 'whithersoever he went' as mentioned in this chapter?
questions.explanation: The repeated statement in 2 Samuel 8:6 and 8:14 that 'the LORD preserved David whithersoever he went' reflects God's faithfulness to His covenant promises, demonstrating the attribute of divine faithfulness.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching is conveyed by David's dedication of spoils (2 Samuel 8:11) and his subjugation of various nations (2 Samuel 8:12)?
options: The doctrine of God's universal reign and the holiness of dedicating spoils to Him
The doctrine of predestination and election
The doctrine of justification by faith
The doctrine of the priesthood of all believers
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of God's universal reign and the holiness of dedicating spoils to Him
questions.explanation: Verses 11 and 12 show David dedicating silver and gold from subdued nations to the LORD, illustrating God's sovereign reign over all nations and the principle that possessions consecrated to God are holy, reflecting His universal lordship (cf. Psalm 22:28).

questions.question: How does the subjugation of Edom and placement of garrisons, along with the LORD's preservation of David (2 Samuel 8:14), reflect on the theological theme of God's control over nations?
options: It shows God’s sovereign control over the rise and fall of nations
It implies nations have ultimate power independent of God
It teaches that military strength alone determines national destiny
It indicates that David acted in rebellion against God
questions.correctAnswer: It shows God’s sovereign control over the rise and fall of nations
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 8:14 shows that David's success in Edom was accompanied by the LORD's preservation, teaching that God sovereignly controls nations' destinies, a key biblical theme (cf. Daniel 4:17).

questions.question: What doctrinal insight about God's justice and judgment can be derived from David's treatment of the Moabites as described in 2 Samuel 8:2?
options: God ordains just punishment with measured mercy
God ignores the sins of nations
God's justice is arbitrary and unmeasured
questions.correctAnswer: God ordains just punishment with measured mercy
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 8:2 describes David measuring Moabites with lines to determine who should die or live, reflecting a divine principle of measured justice coupled with mercy, consistent with God's righteous judgment (cf. Romans 12:19).

questions.question: In light of 2 Samuel 8:4, what theological significance does David's act of 'houghed all the chariot horses' except for a hundred have?
options: It symbolizes the removal of military threat while preserving some for service
It represents an act of cruelty without purpose
It shows David's distrust of horses in warfare
It indicates David's disobedience to God
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes the removal of military threat while preserving some for service
questions.explanation: David's disabling of chariot horses except for a few (2 Samuel 8:4) symbolizes neutralizing enemy power while retaining resources for Israel's use, reflecting God’s justice in subduing enemies yet preserving what is useful for His purposes.

questions.question: How does the sending of Joram by Toi king of Hamath to David (2 Samuel 8:10) reflect the broader biblical theme of God’s providential establishment of His anointed king?
options: It shows recognition of David's God-given authority by surrounding nations
It reveals political alliances based on human diplomacy alone
It indicates Toi’s submission to David as a God-appointed priest
It suggests Toi was unaware of David's conquests
questions.correctAnswer: It shows recognition of David's God-given authority by surrounding nations
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 8:10 shows Toi sending his son to salute and bless David for his victories, indicating God's providential raising of David as king whose authority is acknowledged even by foreign rulers, a theme of God's sovereign rule (cf. Psalm 2).

questions.question: What attribute of God is particularly evident in 2 Samuel 8:7 where David takes the shields of gold from Hadadezer’s servants and brings them to Jerusalem?
options: God's holiness in sanctifying the spoils
God's justice in rewarding His servant
questions.correctAnswer: God's justice in rewarding His servant
questions.explanation: The taking of shields of gold and their transport to Jerusalem (2 Samuel 8:7) illustrates God’s just reward to David for his faithfulness and victory, emphasizing divine justice and blessing on those who serve Him (cf. Psalm 18:50).

questions.question: What synthesis of divine sovereignty and human responsibility is taught by David's military leadership and God's preservation as seen in 2 Samuel 8:16-18 and 2 Samuel 8:6?
options: God sovereignly preserves while humans faithfully execute their roles
God alone acts without human involvement
Human effort alone ensures success without divine aid
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly preserves while humans faithfully execute their roles
questions.explanation: Verses 16-18 describe David’s appointed leaders executing military and administrative duties, while 8:6 emphasizes God's preservation of David, showing a theological synthesis where divine sovereignty and human responsibility coexist harmoniously.

questions.question: What broader redemptive narrative connection is seen in David's conquest of the Philistines and the taking of Methegammah (2 Samuel 8:1)?
options: The foreshadowing of the ultimate victory of the Messiah over evil
The establishment of Israel as a purely military empire
The rejection of God's promises to Israel
The fulfillment of the law of retaliation
questions.correctAnswer: The foreshadowing of the ultimate victory of the Messiah over evil
questions.explanation: David’s victory over the Philistines (2 Samuel 8:1) typologically points to Christ’s ultimate triumph over sin and Satan, aligning with the messianic theme of God's kingdom prevailing over hostile powers (cf. Revelation 19:11-16).

questions.question: How does 2 Samuel 8:9-10 provide apologetic evidence against the claim that David was merely a warlord without divine endorsement?
options: Foreign kings recognized David’s victories as divinely sanctioned
David operated only out of political self-interest
David’s power was based solely on military strength
David was rejected by neighboring nations
questions.correctAnswer: Foreign kings recognized David’s victories as divinely sanctioned
questions.explanation: Verses 9-10 show Toi king of Hamath sending his son to salute and bless David for his victory, evidencing external recognition of David’s God-ordained role, countering sceptical claims of mere human ambition.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about God's providential justice is revealed in David's defeat of Hadadezer and the Syrians (2 Samuel 8:3-5)?
options: God judges and humbles the proud nations opposing His people
God ignores the actions of foreign kings
God always spares the enemies of Israel
God leaves war outcomes to chance
questions.correctAnswer: God judges and humbles the proud nations opposing His people
questions.explanation: David's victories over Hadadezer and the Syrians (2 Samuel 8:3-5) demonstrate God's justice in humbling hostile nations opposing His covenant people, affirming His role as righteous judge (cf. Isaiah 10:5-6).

questions.question: What theological insight about God's blessing on obedience is shown through David's reign and his execution of justice as king (2 Samuel 8:15)?
options: God blesses faithful leadership that administers justice
God’s blessing is unrelated to leadership
Justice is a human invention without divine mandate
David's reign was marked by injustice
questions.correctAnswer: God blesses faithful leadership that administers justice
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 8:15 emphasizes David's righteous rule and justice, illustrating the doctrine that God blesses faithful obedience and just governance, consistent with biblical principles of covenant leadership (cf. Deuteronomy 17:18-20).

questions.question: What synthesis of divine-human partnership in governance is taught by the roles of Joab, Jehoshaphat, Zadok, Ahimelech, and Benaiah as described in 2 Samuel 8:16-18?
options: God ordains human offices to administer His kingdom under His authority
All governance is purely secular without divine involvement
Priests and military leaders had no role in governance
questions.correctAnswer: God ordains human offices to administer His kingdom under His authority
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 8:16-18 lists key officials serving David, showing God's design for structured governance involving both civil and priestly roles in administering His kingdom, demonstrating divine-human partnership in rule.
